title: ThermoWorks Cloud Reading Failure Rate
dataSources: Sourdough monitor (`sourdough:reading`), BBQ/sous-vide probes (`bbq:probe`), fridge/freezer/oven temperature (`kitchen:appliance`), espresso shots (`espresso:shot`), pantry inventory (`pantry:item`), kombucha brew (`kombucha:reading`).
app: ESP32/ESPHome kitchen sensors (sourdough rise, BBQ/sous-vide probes, fridge/freezer temperature), espresso-shot logs, and pantry inventory via MQTT and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=thermoworks:cloud
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(probe_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by probe_name
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often ThermoWorks Cloud reading records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each probe.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize probe_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per probe.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It scans which parts of your ThermoWorks Cloud reading data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
